payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit superseded the initial cycle-life claim, establishing 8,400 cycles as the governing corrected figure. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
